cards.text: Joseph's been sold off to Egypt, and now the story follows one of his brothers: Judah, the one who said sell him instead of killing him (Genesis 37:26–27). About that time, Judah leaves his brothers. He settles near a man named Hirah, an Adullamite.

cards.question: There Judah sees the daughter of a man named Shua and takes her as his wife. Where is Shua from?

cards.text: Then come the boys: Er, then Onan, then Shelah, born at Chezib. Three sons, friend. That's three more hands reaching for the cookie dough before it ever sees an oven.
Judah gets a wife for Er, his firstborn, and her name is Tamar. Remember that name, friend. Write it on your apron.

cards.question: But Er, Judah's firstborn, is wicked in the sight of the LORD. What does the LORD do?

cards.text: Now Tamar is a widow with no children. So Judah turns to his second son, Onan.

cards.question: Judah tells Onan to do his duty as Tamar's brother-in-law and raise up offspring for his ___.

cards.text: But Onan knows something. Any child that comes wouldn't belong to him.

cards.question: So whenever Onan is with Tamar, what does he make sure of?

answers.text: That no child comes for his brother
That the child gets raised as his
That Tamar goes back to her family

cards.question: The LORD sees what Onan did as wicked.

cards.text: So the LORD puts Onan to death as well. That leaves Judah one son: Shelah, the youngest.

cards.question: What does Judah tell his daughter-in-law Tamar to do?

answers.text: Wait at her father's house until Shelah grows up

cards.question: Judah tells Tamar to wait. But what is he thinking about his son Shelah?

answers.text: He may die too like his brothers
He should stay with the flocks

cards.text: So Tamar goes to live in her father's house, and she waits. Friend, I know waiting: I sat in a junk drawer so long the dust had DUST.

A long time passes, and Judah's wife, the daughter of Shua, dies. When he's done mourning, he and his friend Hirah head up to his sheepshearers at Timnah. And somebody tells Tamar her father-in-law is on his way.

cards.question: Tamar hears Judah is headed to Timnah. What has she noticed about Shelah?

answers.text: He's grown but she hasn't been given to him
He's left to work Judah's flocks
He's been promised to someone else

cards.question: So Tamar takes off her widow's garments. What does she do to disguise herself?

answers.text: Covers her face with a veil

cards.text: Then she sits down at the entrance to Enaim, right on the road to Timnah. And she waits for Judah to come by.

cards.question: Judah comes down the road and sees the veiled woman. He knows right away it's his daughter-in-law Tamar.

cards.text: He has NO idea. He thinks she's a prostitute because her face is covered, and he asks to sleep with her, and she asks what he'll give her.

cards.question: Judah has just come from his sheepshearers. What does he promise to send her?

answers.text: A young goat from his flock

cards.text: But Tamar isn't taking a goat on credit. She says only if he leaves her a pledge until he sends it.

cards.question: Judah asks what pledge she wants. What does Tamar ask for?

answers.text: His seal and cord and staff

cards.text: Judah hands over all three, and Tamar becomes pregnant by him. Friend, that's like handing a stranger your wallet, your ID AND your car keys for a goat that hasn't even shown up yet.

cards.question: Then Tamar gets up, leaves and takes off her veil. What does she put back on?

cards.text: Judah sends his friend Hirah with the young goat to collect his things from the woman. Picture Hirah on that road holding a goat, looking around like a man who forgot where he parked.

cards.question: Hirah finds the woman by the road and gets Judah's things back.
Hirah asks the men of that place where the woman by the road at Enaim is. What do they tell him?

answers.text: No such woman was ever here
She left for Timnah that morning

cards.text: So Hirah goes back and tells Judah everything. No woman. No seal. No cord. No staff.

cards.question: Judah tells Hirah to let the woman keep his things. Why?

answers.text: So they won't become a laughingstock
So Hirah won't search any longer
Because he has another seal at home

cards.text: So Judah just walks away from his seal, his cord and his staff. Friend, I shared a junk drawer with a key that never figured out which door it opened, and even THAT key would say, "Man, go get your stuff."
About three months later, someone brings Judah news. His daughter-in-law Tamar has prostituted herself, and now she's pregnant.

cards.question: Judah hears the news about Tamar. What does he order?

answers.text: That she be burned to death

cards.text: As they're bringing her out, Tamar sends a message to her father-in-law. Three months she's been holding onto something, and now she plays it.

cards.question: Tamar's message tells Judah to examine something. What?

answers.text: His seal and cord and staff
The young goat from his flock

cards.text: Her message: "I am pregnant by the man to whom these items belong." And then: "Please examine them. Whose seal and cord and staff are these?"

cards.question: Judah recognizes the items. He says Tamar is more ___ than he is.
Why does Judah say Tamar is more righteous than he is?

answers.text: He didn't give her to Shelah
She paid back the young goat
She never asked him for help

cards.question: After this, Judah has relations with Tamar again.

cards.text: Months go by, and the time comes for Tamar to give birth. And friend, there's a surprise waiting.

cards.question: When the time comes, there are twins in Tamar's womb.

cards.text: As she's giving birth, one of the twins puts out his hand. The midwife grabs a scarlet thread, QUICK.

cards.question: What does the midwife do with the scarlet thread?

answers.text: Ties it around the baby's wrist

cards.text: She announces, "This one came out first." Then that little hand pulls right back in.

cards.question: The twin with the scarlet thread ends up being born first.

cards.text: His brother comes out instead, and the midwife says, "You have broken out first!" Brand new to the world and already cutting in line.

cards.question: What is the twin who broke out first named?

cards.text: Then his brother comes out, scarlet thread still on his wrist, and he's named Zerah. First hand out and he STILL comes in second, which is exactly how I did in every rubber band stretching contest in that junk drawer.
Perez and Zerah. Hold onto those names, friend, because Matthew lists them, born to Judah by Tamar, in the family line of Jesus (Matthew 1:1–3).

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 1 has a dash outside a quotation: "Joseph's been sold off to Egypt, and now the story follows one of his brothers: Judah, the one who said sell him instead of killing him (Genesis 37:26–27). About that time, Judah leaves his brothers. He settles near a man named Hirah, an Adullamite."

rule.text: No em dashes or en dashes to make a sentence longer.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 17 quotes "Man, go get your stuff.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Stop 3, card 13 quotes "This one came out first.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Stop 3, card 18 has a dash outside a quotation: "Perez and Zerah. Hold onto those names, friend, because Matthew lists them, born to Judah by Tamar, in the family line of Jesus (Matthew 1:1–3)."

rule.text: No em dashes or en dashes to make a sentence longer.

findings.problem: The card says Joseph has been sold off to Egypt, but the only reference given is Genesis 37:26–27, which covers Judah's idea to sell him. The sale to Egypt comes from Genesis 37:28 and 37:36, and no reference is given for it.

rule.text: Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: Multiple choice dominates the stop: 5 multiple choice, 1 true or false and 1 fill in the blank.

rule.text: No formula. Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern. No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: The right answer, "Wait at her father's house until Shelah grows up," is much longer and more specific than the wrong answers ("Marry Shelah right away" and "Move in with Judah's household"), so it stands out.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone.

findings.problem: Multiple choice dominates the stop: 7 multiple choice, 2 true or false and no fill in the blank.

rule.text: No formula. Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern. No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: This is not the opening card, but it has 3 sentences. It also has three beats: Judah's wife dies, Judah goes up to Timnah with Hirah, and Tamar is told.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The second sentence has three beats: Judah thinks she's a prostitute, he asks to sleep with her, and she asks what he'll give her.

rule.text: Aim for one beat per story card. Two is the most. If a story card has more than two things happening, split it.

findings.problem: The question says "Judah has just come from his sheepshearers." The text says the opposite. Judah is going up to his sheepshearers at Timnah (38:12–13), and Tamar sits "on the way to Timnah" (38:14).

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: The joke blends the modern comparison (wallet, ID and car keys) with the Bible setting ("for a goat that hasn't even shown up yet").

rule.text: One image only. Never blend the comparison with the Bible setting.

findings.problem: "Looking around like a man who forgot where he parked" signals that Hirah can't find the woman. That gives away the answer to the true or false question on card 13.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The joke blends the modern comparison (a man who forgot where he parked) with the Bible setting (Hirah on that road holding a goat).

rule.text: One image only. Never blend the comparison with the Bible setting.

findings.problem: Hirah asks for "the shrine prostitute" (38:21), but the question calls her "the woman by the road." The right answer, "No such woman was ever here," also changes the text's term and adds "ever" to "has been here."

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The joke adds something new to Papa Dorin's drawer backstory: that he came in second in every rubber band stretching contest. Jokes may only make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: This card tells no new part of the passage. It repeats Perez and Zerah from 38:29–30 and adds a connection to Matthew 1:3, so it works as a closing recap, not as a card that moves the passage along.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage.
